transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nadia Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Whitman (Sable Head of ML Ops), Renee Park (Sable CTO), Luis Martinez (Infra Lead), Amira Shah (Quant)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on cost per token and routing options. Customer runs mixed workloads: nightly batch scoring (high throughput) + low-latency inference for UI. Wants to understand unit economics and what moves the needle (batching, caching, dedicated vs hosted).

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off — this is a cost-econ discovery so we'll focus on per-token, batching, caching, and deployment modes. Ethan and Nadia are here for the heavyweight infra questions.
[00:00:18] Tom Whitman: Yeah thanks, Maya. Quick context: we do nightly scoring for ~20M texts/day, plus a realtime UI path that sees ~5k qps spikes during market opens. Main ask is: what's the cheapest way to run this and when does dedicated make sense vs hosted?
[00:00:36] Ethan Ruiz: Great, so couple quick clarifying q's — typical sequence length for batch jobs? And are the realtime calls short prompts or long chat histories?
[00:00:44] Amira Shah: Batch avg length ~350 tokens, realtime is usually 80-120 tokens but with a 2-turn convo sometimes 250. We also keep some KV cache on the UI when users navigate.
[00:00:58] Renee Park: Also importantly — data residency. The scoring data is mostly EU, so we'd prefer EU region hosting or private.
[00:01:08] Nadia Patel: Noted — private/VPC options can handle that, and Dedicated in EU is also available. For cost comparisons we'll show per-token hosted numbers and then reserved instance math for Dedicated.
[00:01:25] Tom: Ok, show us the numbers, like ballpark per-token for a 13B-ish open model?
[00:01:32] Maya: Sure, ballpark hosted per-token (generation + input) for a 13B quantized model on Redwood Hosted is around $0.0006 - $0.0012 per token depending on seq len and streaming. For embeddings it's different, but focusing on gen. The main levers to lower that are: batching, prefix/KV caching, running a smaller model where quality allows, and Dedicated reserved capacity where unit cost drops with commit.
[00:01:58] Luis Martinez: That hosted range seems... wide. How should we think about the effect of batching on latency for the realtime path? We can't blunt latency during market opens.
[00:02:07] Ethan: Right — we recommend adaptive batching. For realtime we set small max batch windows (e.g., 5-10ms) so P95 latency still meets SLOs, and send larger batches for the nightly scoring. Batching mainly helps throughput jobs; for the nightly 20M texts you'll see 3-5x token efficiency improvements with proper batch sizing and model choice.
[00:02:26] Amira: 3-5x is a big delta — how does caching factor in? We have many repeated prefixes across scored docs.
[00:02:31] Nadia: KV/prefix caching reduces tokens sent and recomputed. If you can cache shared prefixes or use prefix dedupe, effective per-sample tokens drop substantially. For example if you avoid re-sending the same 50-token system prompt per call, that's a 50-token saving *per call*.
[00:02:50] Renee: How do you measure that in billing? Is it per-token sent or per-token generated?
[00:02:55] Maya: Billing is per-token processed — input + output. So reducing input via caching directly lowers billed tokens. Also some customers use delta-encoding in the client to avoid re-sending static context.
[00:03:08] Tom: On Dedicated — what's the commit level where Dedicated becomes cheaper than hosted? We don't want to overcommit if traffic is spiky.
[00:03:16] Ethan: It depends on utilization. Roughly, if you're running sustained tens of thousands of tokens per second or doing large nightly batches, Dedicated with reserved GPUs can reduce per-token cost by ~30-50% vs hosted list price, factoring in model/quantization. But you need to commit to capacity; we offer autoscale and burst to handle spikes, and can structure reserved pools with burst credits.
[00:03:36] Luis: Burst credits sounds useful — how does that work?
[00:03:40] Nadia: You get a baseline reserved throughput; bursts are billed at a slightly higher dedicated overage rate but cheaper than spinning up new transient infra yourselves. It's a middle ground for variability.
[00:03:52] Amira: What about Private / on-prem? We have compliance constraints that might push us there. Does on-prem reduce unit costs?
[00:03:59] Maya: On-prem moves capex to you — per-token software fees can be negotiated, but infra ops cost often dominate. Many teams choose Private for compliance and predictability, not pure unit-cost wins, unless they already have excess GPU capacity.
[00:04:15] Tom: Makes sense. Any guidance on quantization — how much price improvement vs quality drop?
[00:04:22] Ethan: 4-bit quantization for many LLMs yields ~1.5-2x speed/memory gains with minimal quality loss for classification/regex style tasks. For open-ended generation it's model and prompt dependent; we'll recommend tests. 8-bit or mixed can be a safer conservative step.
[00:04:38] Renee: Can Redwood run our internal eval set to show quality delta alongside cost?
[00:04:42] Maya: Absolutely — that's what the benchmark run is for. We can run 50M tokens of your test corpus across hosted and a Dedicated config and provide per-token cost + latency + eval metrics.
[00:04:53] Amira: For the nightly batch 20M/day, what's the estimated monthly cost on hosted vs Dedicated?
[00:04:58] Maya: Quick back-of-envelope — 20M texts * avg 350 tokens = 7B tokens/day, ~210B tokens/month. At $0.0006/token that's $126k/month baseline; with batching + caching that could drop to $40-60k/month depending on how much you can reduce tokens and choose model/quantization. With Dedicated reserved we could get another 30-50% reduction on the after-optimization number — so maybe $25-40k/month. These are roughs; benchmark will give precise numbers.
[00:05:29] Luis: Wow, those are big differences — we need to validate assumptions. What inputs do you need from us for the benchmark?
[00:05:33] Ethan: Sample dataset (anonymized), target SLOs for realtime (P95), typical prompt templates, and any constraints (EU residency). We'll also want load profiles for spikes.
[00:05:47] Tom: On security — SOC2, SSO, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and audit logs per request?
[00:05:53] Nadia: Yes — Private and Dedicated offer KMS integrations and per-request audit logs. Hosted supports envelope encryption and SOC2 compliance; for full CMK we recommend Dedicated or Private depending on your needs.
[00:06:04] Renee: For EU residency do you have EU-hosted Dedicated regions?
[00:06:08] Maya: Yes, we have EU regions and can place Dedicated pools there. Private can also be deployed into your VPC in EU.
[00:06:15] Amira: Any hidden costs we should watch for — e.g., cold-starts, KV storage, or egress fees?
[00:06:20] Ethan: Good call — egress is standard cloud egress. KV cache storage is typically small but for very large prefix caches it can add up; we can include that in the benchmark estimate. Cold-starts are mitigated in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can see instance spin-ups at low utilization but we manage warm pools for commercial customers.
[00:06:39] Tom: How do we instrument to measure real cost impact of batching/caching on our side?
[00:06:44] Nadia: We provide per-route token breakdowns in the Console with token-level and cost-level attribution, plus tracing hooks. You can run A/B tests with and without caching to see delta.
[00:06:54] Renee: Competitors — are you typically cheaper than OpenAI for bulk scoring?
[00:06:58] Maya: For bulk scoring especially with Dedicated we generally see lower unit economics vs managed competitors because of optimized runtime, batching, and reserved pricing. But specifics depend on model family and commitment. We'll include competitor comparisons in the pricing doc.
[00:07:12] Amira: Anything else — do you do auto-quantization suggestions?
[00:07:15] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize provides model/quantization recommendations by workload. It looks at your eval metrics and suggests quant profiles and model variants that trade quality vs cost.
[00:07:25] Tom: Ok good. On SLA — if we move to Dedicated and commit, what's the SLA for latency/uptime?
[00:07:30] Maya: We publish SLA tiers; Dedicated includes higher uptime guarantees and latency SLOs depending on config. We'll surface the SLA doc in the follow-up.
[00:07:40] Renee: To recap, we want: pricing sheet, benchmark run, SOC2 + KMS docs, and a proposed Dedicated sizing with burst plan.
[00:07:47] Maya: Yep — I'll send the pricing sheet and proposed SOW outline. Ethan will schedule the benchmark run and share infra requirements. Tom, you said you'd confirm residency?
[00:07:56] Tom: Yes I'll confirm by Monday.
[00:07:59] Maya: Great. Any final quick q's?
[00:08:03] Luis: One — for the realtime UI path, if we add a small local prefix cache + small Dedicated pool, could we keep latency P95 under 200ms?
[00:08:10] Ethan: Likely yes — with a tuned model and small batch windows, P95 down to ~120-200ms is achievable depending on seq length. We'll test in the benchmark.
[00:08:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs + scheduling.
[00:08:24] [call continues with scheduling logistics and some small clarifications] 
[00:10:02] Maya: (wrap) next steps captured.
